# gen-ai-prv

A small Go command-line client for OpenAI's [Content Provenance API](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/content-provenance). It checks an image, audio file, or PDF for supported OpenAI provenance signals.

**This is not a general-purpose AI detector.** A `not_detected` result does not prove that content was made by a person or that it was not generated by AI. The API currently checks supported C2PA and SynthID signals; it does not accept arbitrary text.

## Requirements

- Go 1.22+
- An OpenAI API key with access to the Content Provenance API

## Build and use

```sh
go build -o gen-ai-prv .
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-api-key"
./gen-ai-prv ./image.png
```

Start the built-in web interface:

```sh
./gen-ai-prv serve
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:8080>. The page supports selecting or dragging
multiple files into the file chooser and checks them one at a time. Each
frontend API request contains exactly one file. The page serves its HTML and
CSS from the executable (no extra frontend files are needed). It uses
`OPENAI_API_KEY` or a key saved in the OS keyring. Configure the server with
`--host`, `--port`, `--tls-cert`, and `--tls-key`; for example:

```sh
./gen-ai-prv serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9090
./gen-ai-prv serve --host example.com --port 8443 --tls-cert server.crt --tls-key server.key
```

Use `--host :` to listen on all interfaces; Go's TCP listener uses a dual-stack
wildcard where supported, accepting both IPv4 and IPv6 connections.

TLS is enabled when both certificate and key are provided. Settings may also be
provided in `gen-ai-prv.yaml` in the current directory, `~/.config/gen-ai-prv/`,
or the home directory. Use `--config path/to/config.yaml` to select another
file. For example:

```yaml
host: 127.0.0.1
port: 8443
tls-cert: server.crt
tls-key: server.key
```

CLI flags override configuration-file values; `GEN_AI_PRV_HOST`,
`GEN_AI_PRV_PORT`, `GEN_AI_PRV_TLS_CERT`, and `GEN_AI_PRV_TLS_KEY` environment
variables are also supported. The deprecated `--addr` flag remains available.
Only bind to a network interface you trust.
At startup, the server reports whether it selected the key from
`OPENAI_API_KEY` or the OS keyring.

Pass multiple paths to check several files in one run:

```sh
./gen-ai-prv ./image.png ./audio.mp3 ./document.pdf
```

Each file is checked with a separate API request. The text output labels each
result with its file path. With multiple files, `-json` prints an array of
objects containing each `file` path and its API `response`; with one file, it
continues to print the API response directly.

`OPENAI_API_KEY` takes precedence when set. Otherwise, the CLI uses a key saved
in the OS keyring; if no key is saved, it prompts for one without echoing it
and stores it in the keyring for future runs.

## Container

Build the image with Podman (or Docker):

```sh
podman build -t gen-ai-prv -f Containerfile .
# Docker:
docker build -t gen-ai-prv -f Containerfile .
```

The image uses `scratch` and runs as a non-root user. Pass the API key through
the environment; the container does not have an OS keyring. To check a local
file, mount its directory read-only:

```sh
podman run --rm -e OPENAI_API_KEY -v "$PWD:/data:ro" gen-ai-prv /data/image.png
```

To start the web interface, bind it to all container interfaces and publish its
port:

```sh
podman run --rm -e OPENAI_API_KEY -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 gen-ai-prv serve --host 0.0.0.0
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8080>. Use `docker run` in place of `podman run` with
Docker.

Print the full API response as JSON:

```sh
./gen-ai-prv -json ./document.pdf
```

Supported extensions are PNG, JPG/JPEG, WebP, GIF, MP3, Opus, AAC, FLAC, WAV, PCM, and PDF. Uploads are limited to 50 MiB. Audio must be 60 seconds or shorter after decoding. The CLI sets the media type from the file extension (Opus uses `audio/ogg`) and uploads the file with a generic ASCII filename to support paths containing spaces or Unicode.

The command prints a concise colored provenance-signal result followed by the detailed summary by default (green when no signal is detected, red when one is detected; color is used in a terminal) and returns a nonzero exit status for usage, file, or API errors. It does not treat `not_detected` as proof that content is human-created.
